land.text: Yiwu round Dingzhou, held by Wang Chuzhi from 900 and made a principality (Prince of Beiping) by Zhu Wen in 907

predecessors.note: Wang Chuzhi governed Yiwu as a Tang then Later Liang circuit from 900; de jure independence dates from 910.

land.text: Ding Prefecture (Dingzhou), whose gates Wang Du's officer Ma Rangneng opened to the Later Tang in early 929

rulers.name: Wang Chuzhi (Prince of Beiping)
rulers.title: Prince of Beiping 907-921
rulers.note: Military governor from 900; arrested by his son Wang Du in 921 and died 6 February 923.

rulers.name: Wang Du
rulers.title: military governor of Yiwu
rulers.note: Overthrew his father in 921; committed suicide in early 929.

correction.text: Yiwu Circuit, 'around modern Baoding, Hebei', capital Dingzhou

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. The page gives the territory as 'Yiwu, around modern Baoding, Hebei' and says Yi and Ding prefectures are not described as his holdings; the 70 km circle (about 15,000 km2) is the researcher's reading. No area on the page.

region.text: Yiwu Circuit, 'around modern Baoding, Hebei', capital Dingzhou

ledger.note: 910: Wang Chuzhi goes independent. 'Later Liang moves against Wushun's Shen and Ji prefectures. Wang Rong breaks away, and Wang Chuzhi becomes independent de jure' (Prince of Beiping since 907; he allied with Jin and Zhao in 911).
921: Wang Du takes over. When Wang Rong was killed he and the secretary He Zhaoxun arrested Wang Chuzhi, killed his other sons and close associates; Li Cunxu approved the takeover.

region.text: Yiwu Circuit, 'around modern Baoding, Hebei', capital Dingzhou

ledger.note: 929: Later Tang takes Dingzhou. Wang Du kept Yiwu in 'de facto independence'; in early 929 his officer Ma Rangneng 'opened the gates of Ding Prefecture' to the Later Tang forces and Wang Du committed suicide, ending the campaign.

wars.name: Battle of Boxiang (911)
wars.outcome: Wang Chuzhi's army helped crush the Later Liang forces in spring 911; Liu Shouguang's Yan attacked Yiwu in the winter of 911.

wars.name: Later Tang campaign against Wang Du

zones.text: Yiwu Circuit, 'around modern Baoding, Hebei', capital Dingzhou

wars.outcome: Later Tang forces besieged Wang Du in 928-929; Ma Rangneng opened the gates of Dingzhou in early 929 and Wang Du killed himself.
wars.note: The Mingzong page dates only the spring 928 accusation (An Chonghui against Wang Jianli) and the early 929 end; the start of the campaign is the researcher's reading.

certainty.note: Circuit frontiers, no line on the page.

sources.title: Wang Chuzhi
sources.note: Yiwu from 900, Prince of Beiping 907, independence 910, Boxiang 911, Wang Du 921, capital Dingzhou.

sources.title: Emperor Mingzong of Later Tang
sources.note: Spring 928 and early 929: Wang Du, de facto independence, the fall of Dingzhou.

notes: New state (Cliopatria lacks it); requested by the former-jin and later-tang dossiers as 'Yiwu (Wang Chuzhi, Dingzhou)'. Open points: (1) the Wang Chuzhi page has him in the Tang's Yiwu from 900 (de facto) with de jure independence 910; 900-910 is not drawn; (2) the later-tang dossier's Wang Du war entry should name yiwu-five-dynasties as belligerent and carry a gain 929; (3) Wang Chuzhi's death is 6 February 923 on the page but the page puts Wang Du's visit in 'spring', an inconsistency; (4) Yiwu's 11th-century successors are out of scope.
